```{r packages}
# install.packages(c("tidyverse", "rsample", "skimr", "scales"))
library(tidyverse)
library(rsample)   # stratified train/test split
library(skimr)     # compact data summaries
library(scales)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
y_cols <- c(no = "grey65", yes = "#1f77b4")
```

# Download the data to `data/raw/`

The UCI zip contains two nested zips (`bank.zip` and `bank-additional.zip`). We use `bank-full.csv` (45,211 rows, 16 predictors + `y`), which is inside `bank.zip`. The download is skipped if the file is already present, so re-knitting doesn't hit the server each time.

```{r download}
data_url <- "https://archive.ics.uci.edu/static/public/222/bank+marketing.zip"
raw_dir  <- file.path("data", "raw")
dir.create(raw_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

zip_path <- file.path(raw_dir, "bank+marketing.zip")

if (!file.exists(zip_path)) {
  options(timeout = max(300, getOption("timeout")))   # slow connections
  download.file(data_url, destfile = zip_path, mode = "wb")
}

# Unzip the outer archive, then the inner bank.zip
unzip(zip_path, exdir = raw_dir)
inner_zip <- file.path(raw_dir, "bank.zip")
if (file.exists(inner_zip)) unzip(inner_zip, exdir = raw_dir)

raw_csv <- list.files(raw_dir, pattern = "^bank-full\\.csv$",
                      recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)[1]
stopifnot("bank-full.csv not found after unzipping" = !is.na(raw_csv))

raw_csv
list.files(raw_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

# Wrangle and clean, saving to `data/processed/`

The raw file is **semicolon-delimited**. Cleaning steps:

1.  Read with the correct delimiter.
2.  Convert text columns to factors, with `y` levelled `no`/`yes` and `month` in calendar order.
3.  Recode the sentinel `pdays = -1` ("never previously contacted") as a logical flag `prev_contacted` plus `pdays` set to `NA`. As a number, −1 would wrongly read as "very recently contacted".
4.  Keep `"unknown"` as its own factor level. Whether it is informative is checked in the EDA, and any imputation happens later, after the split.
5.  Drop `duration` (length of the last call). It is only known after the call ends, so it leaks the outcome.

```{r read-raw}
bank_raw <- read_delim(raw_csv, delim = ";", show_col_types = FALSE)
dim(bank_raw)

```

```{r}
glimpse(bank_raw)
```

```{r clean}
month_levels <- c("jan", "feb", "mar", "apr", "may", "jun",
                  "jul", "aug", "sep", "oct", "nov", "dec")

bank_clean <- bank_raw |>
  mutate(
    across(where(is.character), as.factor),
    y      = factor(y, levels = c("no", "yes")),
    month  = factor(month, levels = month_levels),
    prev_contacted = pdays != -1,
    pdays  = na_if(pdays, -1)
  ) |>
  select(-duration)

# Sanity checks
stopifnot(nrow(bank_clean) == nrow(bank_raw),
          !anyNA(bank_clean$y),
          all(!is.na(bank_clean$month)))
sum(duplicated(bank_clean))   # count of exact duplicate rows

glimpse(bank_clean)
```

```{r save-processed}
processed_dir <- file.path("data", "processed")
dir.create(processed_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

write_csv(bank_clean, file.path(processed_dir, "bank_clean.csv"))
```

# Split into training and test sets

The split happens **before** any EDA or preprocessing, so nothing we learn from the data is influenced by the test set. Because `y` is imbalanced, the split is **stratified on `y`**, which keeps the yes/no proportion the same in both sets. A seed makes it reproducible.

```{r split}
set.seed(552)
bank_split <- initial_split(bank_clean, prop = 0.75, strata = y)
bank_train <- training(bank_split)
bank_test  <- testing(bank_split)

write_csv(bank_train, file.path(processed_dir, "bank_train.csv"))
write_csv(bank_test,  file.path(processed_dir, "bank_test.csv"))

tibble(set = c("train", "test"),
       n   = c(nrow(bank_train), nrow(bank_test)),
       yes_rate = c(mean(bank_train$y == "yes"), mean(bank_test$y == "yes")))
```

# Exploratory data analysis (training data only)

## Overview

```{r skim}
skim(bank_train)
```

## Target variable

```{r target}
bank_train |>
  count(y) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))
```

Only about 12% of clients subscribed, so the classes are imbalanced. Accuracy alone would be a misleading metric for a model, because predicting "no" for everyone would already be about 88% accurate.

## Missing and `"unknown"` values

```{r missing}
bank_train |>
  summarise(across(everything(),
                   ~ sum(is.na(.) | (is.factor(.) & . == "unknown")))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "n_missing") |>
  filter(n_missing > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(n_missing))
```

`pdays` is `NA` for clients who were never contacted before, and `poutcome` is mostly `"unknown"` for the same reason. `contact`, `education` and `job` have smaller numbers of unknowns.

## Numeric predictors by outcome

```{r numeric-summary}
num_vars <- c("age", "balance", "day", "campaign", "pdays", "previous")

bank_train |>
  select(all_of(num_vars), y) |>
  pivot_longer(-y, names_to = "variable") |>
  group_by(variable, y) |>
  summarise(mean   = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd     = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(., 1)))
```

## Categorical predictors by outcome

Proportion of clients who subscribed in each group:

```{r cat-summary}
bank_train |>
  group_by(poutcome) |>
  summarise(n = n(), prop_yes = mean(y == "yes"))

bank_train |>
  group_by(contact) |>
  summarise(n = n(), prop_yes = mean(y == "yes"))
```

# Visualizations of the training data

## Histograms of the numeric predictors

```{r viz-hist, fig.height=6}
bank_train |>
  select(all_of(num_vars)) |>
  pivot_longer(everything()) |>
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free") +
  labs(title = "Distributions of numeric predictors (training data)",
       x = NULL, y = "Count")
```

## Boxplots of numeric predictors by outcome

```{r viz-box, fig.height=6}
bank_train |>
  select(all_of(num_vars), y) |>
  pivot_longer(-y) |>
  ggplot(aes(y, value, fill = y)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = y_cols, guide = "none") +
  labs(title = "Numeric predictors by subscription outcome (training data)",
       x = "Subscribed", y = NULL)
```

## Subscription by categorical predictor

```{r viz-bar, fig.height=8}
bank_train |>
  select(job, marital, education, contact, month, poutcome, y) |>
  pivot_longer(-y, values_to = "level") |>
  ggplot(aes(y = level, fill = y)) +
  geom_bar(position = "fill") +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = y_cols) +
  labs(title = "Proportion subscribing within each group (training data)",
       x = "Proportion", y = NULL, fill = "Subscribed")
```

# Summary of EDA findings

- **Class imbalance:** about 12% "yes".
- **Skewed numerics:** `balance`, `campaign` and `previous` have long right tails and outliers, and may need transforming in preprocessing.
- **`poutcome`:** clients whose previous campaign was a success subscribe much more often.
- **`"unknown"` values:** these are concentrated in `poutcome` and `contact`.
